about: The hill-climb tracker on the dashboard's front page (RAY-237, plans/rendering-cpu-roadmap.md in the Captain drive).

metrics: one chart each. lower is true when smaller is better. budget draws a line (the 16.7 ms 60 fps frame), reference a shaded band (plain three.js). state metrics (thermal) take a text state instead of a value. pending is shown while a metric has no points.

points: one reading per series per step, in the order they landed. at is the x-axis label: a PR ("#290"), a release tag ("kong-v1.1.0") or a phase target. kind is measured (read on a real machine, n >= 1), estimate (expected from a profile or model) or target (where a phase aims). low and high give a range. build is the commit or release measured, n the run count, method how it was read, source where the raw data lives.
Add a point with npx tsx tools/dashboard/hillclimb-add.mts (see its header); it checks the whole file before writing. build.mts refuses to build the page from a bad file.
plain: My hill climb on CPU, power and smoothness. One core runs flat out while I walk through town on my RTX laptop, because the main thread needs more than the 16.7 ms a 60 fps frame allows. Each step below is one merged PR or release, measured on the same route, so you can watch the lines move.

main-ms.label: Main thread per frame
main-ms.plain: Unprofiled main-thread time per frame on the seeded tour route (High, 1080p). Under the line, the core gets idle time every frame.

us-per-draw.label: JavaScript per draw
us-per-draw.plain: Render submit time divided by draw calls on the tour. The shaded band is what plain three.js r186 spends per draw in a microbenchmark.

reference.label: plain three.js
reference.source: 1,500-mesh microbenchmark, cloud x86, Chrome on SwiftShader, 3 runs; Captain drive reports/KONG-89.md

power-w.label: Power over a practice match
power-w.plain: CPU, GPU and package watts from powermetrics over a full practice match on Honu. Release to release, this should not go up.
power-w.pending: The power baseline on Honu runs now; its first points land from handoffs/power-baseline/.

thermal.label: Thermal state over a practice match
thermal.plain: macOS thermal pressure (or fan speed) at the end of a full practice match on Honu.

fps.label: Frames per second
fps.plain: Median frame rate on the same scene. The Mac mini in Chrome is held at 60 by its display.

points.source: Captain drive reports/KONG-89.md; tours in project drive handoffs/KONG-68/{rtx-d3d11,mini-metal}/tour-{1,2,3}.json
